reactions._note: These reactions extend hopanoids beyond diplopterol and are not in MetaCyc.

reactions.name: adenosylhopane synthesis
reactions.metacyc_status: not in MetaCyc; required for hopanoid side-chain biosynthesis

reactions.name: bacteriohopanetetrol synthesis
reactions.notes: Enzyme not identified. May involve ring opening of the ribose.
references: Belin et al. 2018 Nat Rev Microbiol

reactions.name: BHT-cyclitol-ether synthesis
reactions.enzyme_name: hopanoid biosynthesis-associated radical SAM cyclitol synthase

reactions.name: 2-methyl-BHT synthesis
reactions.notes: Can also act on other hopanoids (diplopterol, etc.) but BHT is primary substrate
reactions.biomarker_relevance: 2-methylhopanes - formerly cyanobacterial marker, now known in alphaproteobacteria, nitrite oxidizers

reactions._note: These connect to archaeol (CPD-15250) from PWY-6349

reactions.name: GDGT-0 synthesis
reactions.notes: Joins two archaeol molecules by forming two C-C bonds between terminal carbons of phytanyl chains.
reactions.biomarker_relevance: GDGT-0 is precursor to all cyclized GDGTs used in TEX86 paleothermometry

reactions.name: GDGT C-7 cyclization
reactions.mechanism: radical SAM cyclopentane ring formation at C-7
reactions.notes: Introduces 1-4 cyclopentane rings at C-7 position. Product represents GDGT-1 through GDGT-4 (all C-7 cyclized isomers).
reactions.biomarker_relevance: TEX86 paleothermometry relies on relative abundances of cyclized GDGTs

reactions.name: GDGT C-3 cyclization
reactions.mechanism: radical SAM cyclopentane ring formation at C-3
reactions.notes: Acts on C-7 cyclized GDGTs to add rings at C-3 position. Product represents GDGT-5 through GDGT-8 (highly cyclized isomers).
reactions.biomarker_relevance: Highly cyclized GDGTs found in hyperthermophilic archaea

reactions.name: GMGT synthesis
reactions.mechanism: radical SAM cross-linking of biphytanyl chains
reactions.notes: Also known as H-GDGT bridge synthase (Hbs). Creates covalent bridge between two biphytanyl chains within GDGT.

reactions.name: hydroxyarchaeol synthesis
references: Mori et al. 2015 Biochem Biophys Res Comm
reactions.notes: MA0127 hydratase acts on the unsaturated DGGGP precursor (BIS-GERANYLGERANYLGLYCEROL-PHOSPHATE), hydroxylating the 2',3'-double bond of one geranylgeranyl chain. The subsequent geranylgeranyl reductase (GGR) reduction to fully saturated hydroxyarchaeol is implicit. MA0127 orthologs found in Methanosarcinales, Methanococcales, some Methanobacteriales.
reactions.biomarker_relevance: sn-2-hydroxyarchaeol and sn-3-hydroxyarchaeol are diagnostic for methanogenic archaea in sediments

reactions.name: macrocyclic archaeol synthesis
reactions.mechanism: radical SAM intramolecular C-C bond formation
reactions.notes: Same Tes enzyme as GDGT-0 synthesis (SUPP-RXN-TES) but acting intramolecularly on a single archaeol molecule to form a 36-membered macrocyclic ring. Side product of Tes alongside GDGT-0.
reactions.biomarker_relevance: macrocyclic archaeol found in archaeal membranes, indicates Tes activity

reactions.name: GMGT methylation
reactions.notes: Gmm preferentially methylates GMGT substrates over GDGT substrates. Can produce mono-, di-, or tri-methylated GMGT. Simplified here as single methylation step.
reactions.biomarker_relevance: methylated GMGTs found in deep subsurface and hot spring environments

reactions.name: GDGT desaturation
reactions.notes: B12-rSAM enzyme that anaerobically introduces double bonds in the saturated biphytanyl chains of GDGTs. In effect, this reverses the earlier saturation by geranylgeranyl reductase. Identified in Candidatus Bathyarchaeota B1_G15, validated by heterologous expression in M. acetivorans and T. kodakarensis. Genomically associated with Hgs.

reactions.name: hydroxy-GDGT synthesis
reactions.notes: Non-rSAM AttH-like hydratase that hydrates double bond(s) introduced by Ted to form OH-GDGTs. Genomically associated with Ted in Candidatus Bathyarchaeota B1_G15.
reactions.biomarker_relevance: OH-GDGTs are the basis of the RI-OH' sea surface temperature proxy, complementing TEX86

reactions.name: GDGT methylation
reactions.notes: Two B12-rSAM GDGT methylases with different substrate specificities identified in S. acidocaldarius and T. aggregans. Distinct from Gmm (which preferentially methylates GMGTs). GDGT methylation increases in response to membrane-destabilizing agents (penicillin G, hexanoic acid). Simplified as single reaction.
reactions.biomarker_relevance: methylated GDGTs found in thermophilic archaea; methylation level responsive to environmental stress

reactions._comment: Triterpenoid reactions without a MetaCyc pathway (1 reaction)
reactions._note: This reaction is in MetaCyc but not assigned to a pathway; it is listed here so that it connects to the network.

reactions.name: isoarborinol synthesis
reactions.products_metacyc_note: isoarborinol is in MetaCyc as CPD-15243; reaction RXN-14392 is not assigned to a pathway
reactions.mechanism: oxidosqualene cyclization (chair-boat-chair conformation) to pentacyclic arborane skeleton
reactions.notes: Two phylogenetically distinct OSCs catalyze this reaction: plant isoarborinol synthase (IAS, e.g. Oryza sativa) and bacterial eudoraenol synthase (EUS, Eudoraea adriatica). Both use 2,3-oxidosqualene as substrate via chair-boat-chair conformation. The network connection is the same for both enzymes (single-step cyclization from EPOXYSQUALENE), so the reaction is recorded once. MetaCyc has this reaction as RXN-14392, not assigned to a pathway.
reactions.biomarker_relevance: Isoarborinol (arborane skeleton) preserved as molecular fossil in sedimentary rocks; previously attributed only to angiosperms, now known in marine bacteria (Banta et al. 2017)
reactions.metacyc_status: in MetaCyc as RXN-14392, not assigned to a pathway

reactions._note: For isorenieratene and okenone synthesis. The cyclization (cruA/cruB equivalent) is in MetaCyc as RXN1F-150/151.

reactions.name: isorenieratene synthesis
reactions.products_metacyc_note: isorenieratene not in MetaCyc (phi,phi-carotene with both rings aromatic)
reactions.mechanism: desaturation and methyl group migration to form aromatic phi-rings on both ends
reactions.biomarker_relevance: Isorenieratane - diagnostic for brown GSB, indicates deep photic zone euxinia
reactions.metacyc_status: not in MetaCyc; MetaCyc RXN-10648 forms one chi ring only
reactions.note: MetaCyc RXN-10648 produces beta,chi-carotene (CPD-11456) with one aromatic ring. Isorenieratene has both rings aromatized.

reactions.name: okenone C-4 ketolation
reactions.notes: Forms the characteristic chi-ring keto group

reactions.name: okenone chi-ring formation
reactions.biomarker_relevance: Okenane - diagnostic for purple sulfur bacteria (Chromatiaceae), indicates shallow photic zone euxinia

reactions._note: Neoproterozoic biomarkers, not in MetaCyc. The substrate is isofucosterol (CPD-4127).

reactions.name: 24-isopropylcholesterol synthesis
reactions.notes: Adds methyl group to existing 24-ethylidene group to form 24-isopropyl. The stereochemistry yields the isopropyl (branched) configuration. Substrate is isofucosterol (CPD-4127), a C29 sterol.
reactions.biomarker_relevance: 24-isopropylcholestane is a Neoproterozoic biomarker attributed to demosponges, found in sediments back to ~635 Ma.
reactions.metacyc_status: not in MetaCyc; sponge and symbiont pathway

reactions.name: 24-n-propylcholesterol synthesis
reactions.mechanism: C-24 methylation forming n-propyl group (linear configuration)
reactions.notes: Same substrate as isopropyl reaction but different stereochemistry yields n-propyl (linear) instead of isopropyl (branched). Distinguished from 24-isopropylcholesterol by GC-MS fragmentation patterns.
reactions.biomarker_relevance: 24-n-propylcholestane distinguishes pelagophyte algae from demosponges in Neoproterozoic-Cambrian biomarker records.

reactions.name: tetrahymanol synthesis from hopene (bacterial route)
reactions.mechanism: E-ring expansion converting 5-membered hopanoid E-ring to 6-membered gammacerane ring
references: Kleemann et al. 1990 Journal of General Microbiology
Hartner et al. 2005 FEMS Microbiology Letters
Banta et al. 2015 PNAS (bacterial STC homologs)
reactions.notes: Alternative bacterial route to tetrahymanol via hopanoid intermediate. The eukaryotic route (SQUALENE → TETRAHYMANOL, EC 4.2.1.123) is already in MetaCyc. This bacterial route explains why tetrahymanol is found in some prokaryotes despite being classically associated with ciliates.
reactions.biomarker_relevance: Gammacerane - biomarker for water column stratification, ciliates, and some bacteria.
reactions.metacyc_status: not in MetaCyc; the eukaryotic route is in MetaCyc as EC 4.2.1.123

reactions.name: coprostanol synthesis (microbial cholesterol reduction)
reactions.products_metacyc_note: MetaCyc compound CPD-21037 (coprostanol); the reaction is not in MetaCyc
reactions.mechanism: reduction of Δ5 double bond to 5β-configuration
references: Eyssen et al. 1973 European J Biochemistry
Freier et al. 1994 J Lipid Research
reactions.notes: Produced by anaerobic gut bacteria. Reduction produces 5β-stanol configuration.
reactions.biomarker_relevance: Coprostanol is a fecal biomarker used in environmental studies to trace sewage contamination. 5β-stanols vs 5α-stanols distinguish biogenic from diagenetic steranes.
reactions.metacyc_status: not in MetaCyc; the compound is in MetaCyc, the reduction is not
